reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates N-doping forming a Pt-rich shell with M–N bonds on an HEA electrocatalyst, improving durability and activity for the oxygen reduction reaction. However, it does not address automotive exhaust conditions (CO/hydrocarbon oxidation, poisoning by H2O/NO, low-temperature operation), so the premise that these benefits apply to the proposed exhaust catalysis context is unsupported.
premises: Nitrogen doping of a near-equiatomic HEA catalyst can form a Pt-rich surface shell with M–N bonds.
M–N bonds stabilize the catalyst structure and enhance corrosion resistance.
The Pt-rich shell with M–N bonds improves catalytic activity and long-term durability.
These structural and performance benefits are achievable without increasing platinum-group metal content.
The cited evidence from electrocatalysis is directly transferable to automotive exhaust catalysis conditions.
